key_insight: An LLM-agent system can autonomously orchestrate reusable calibration “Skills” to bring up a 112-qubit superconducting processor with expert-like decisions and self-healing behavior.
engineering_relevance: This shows a path to scaling quantum hardware operation by replacing brittle manual scripts with auditable, transferable automation for complex calibration workflows.
method: Three-phase human-in-the-loop distillation of expert tacit knowledge into reusable Skills
Fine-tuning a large language model on validated calibration trajectories
Each Skill uses a decision tree with parameterized measurements, acceptance criteria, and audit records
evidence_signal: The system autonomously calibrated 108 of 112 qubits in 4.7 hours, with a reported 4–5× speedup over manual calibration and 14/16 agreement versus experts on a 16-qubit subset.
watch_item: Autonomy still depends on device-specific low-level control interfaces and some qubits remained uncalibrated, so robustness and portability need careful validation.
paper_title: Vibe Calibration: Autonomous Bring-up of a 112-Qubit Superconducting Quantum Processor by a Skill-Orchestrating Language Agent
